overview: School psychologists help students who struggle with learning, behavior or mental health. They give and interpret tests, write reports for teachers and parents, plan support and report safety concerns to the right authorities. O*NET rates knowledge of psychology at 5 out of 5 for this job and speaking at 4.62. Most hold a specialist degree: 58% report a post-master's certificate and 23% a master's degree, plus a state credential. The BLS May 2025 median is $95,990 across 63,940 jobs. Deadlines for evaluations are tight and conflict with families can happen, but schedules follow the school year.
pay: School psychologists earn a median of $95,990, and the top 10% earn $142,330 or more. California pays the most at $127,780, 33% above the national figure, followed by Colorado at $124,770. New York has the most jobs, 9,070, with a median of $106,550. Mississippi has the lowest state median, $61,070.

faq.q: How much do school psychologists make?
faq.a: The BLS May 2025 median is $95,990 a year. The middle half earn between $77,470 and $120,310. California ($127,780) and Colorado ($124,770) have the highest state medians, while Arkansas ($64,030) and Mississippi ($61,070) pay the least. Pay often follows district salary schedules.

faq.q: How long does it take to become a school psychologist?
faq.a: Most complete a specialist-level graduate program of about 3 years, including a supervised internship. In O*NET data, 58% of school psychologists report a post-master's certificate, 23% a master's degree and 15% a professional degree. A state credential or license is also required.

faq.q: What does a school psychologist do?
faq.a: A school psychologist evaluates students, interprets test results and writes reports for teachers, parents and special education teams. O*NET rates reading comprehension and speaking at 4.62 out of 5 and active listening at 4.5. Much of the job is meeting with families and staff.

faq.q: What jobs are similar to school psychologist?
faq.a: The closest moves are secondary special education teachers (83% match), Marriage and Family Therapists (82%) and Speech-Language Pathologists (81%), based on O*NET 31.0. Genetic Counselors are also an 81% match and earn $100,040, 4% more, according to BLS May 2025.
